title: Count and Circle Worksheets for Kindergarten – Free Printable Activities
intro: Teach selecting a given number from a larger collection.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Read the requested count aloud. Have the student circle pictures one at a time and stop when that count is reached.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Try this together: put seven counters on a table and say, “Please give me three.” Let the child move one counter at a time while saying “one, two, three.” Stop and count the selected group to check.

On the worksheet, a circle plays the same role as moving a counter. Each circle identifies one selected object. The remaining objects stay outside the selected group.

Ask your student

How will you know when to stop circling?

If your student needs help

If the student circles every picture, count the selected group separately from the whole collection.
